Hi David —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: for EU transfers where Greenway is the controller and Redwood is a processor, the controller-to-processor SCCs are the right starting point (the module equivalent in the 2021 SCCs). For UK transfers, we typically execute the EU SCCs plus the UK Addendum (the UK Addendum is required to mirror UK adequacy requirements).

That said, there are a few follow-ups for our legal team to confirm appendix content and any scoping needed for subprocessors. Looping in Marissa and Karthik to provide the formal recommendation and a draft package (DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum) and a comparison sheet for your counsel.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: confirm module wording and whether any custom clauses are needed for Greenway's use case.
- Karthik: confirm Appendix 1/2 items we need from Greenway (purposes, categories, transfer locations).
- David: if you have a preferred signature workflow (DocuSign/hand-signed) and target date, please share.

I'll follow up after legal weighs in.

Jordan / David —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed Greenway's summary and drafted recommended language and a module map (attached: SCCs_Module_Comparison_Greenway.xlsx and UK_Addendum_Draft.pdf). High-level guidance below.

1) EU transfers (Greenway = Controller, Redwood = Processor)
- Execute the Controller-to-Processor SCCs (the "C2P" set in the 2021 SCC framework). This aligns with the controller/processor relationship and allows us to populate Appendix 1/2.
- Populate Appendix 1 (description of transfer) with customer-specific details (processing activities, categories of data, legal basis). We'll need Greenway to confirm these items.

2) UK transfers
- For personal data flows to/from the UK, execute the EU SCCs plus the UK Addendum (our usual approach). The Addendum mirrors UK GDPR expectations and is required for robust transfer coverage post‑Brexit.
- If transfers route through third countries, flag those locations in Appendix 2 and consider additional safeguards (e.g., encryption in transit, limited retention).

3) HIPAA overlap / BAA
- HIPAA obligations are separate. If Greenway is processing PHI and expects Redwood to act as a business associate under US law, we will need a standalone BAA (Business Associate Agreement). Our commercial DPA does not substitute for a BAA. Please confirm whether your use case requires a BAA; if so we'll route to our compliance team for a BAA template and timeline.

4) Practical execution and timing
- We recommend delivering: Redwood DPA (v3.2) + C2P SCCs with Appendix placeholders + UK Addendum. I attached a draft DPA and a comparison spreadsheet showing differences between the C2P and alternative module choices.
- Target timeline: review & populate appendices (1 week), internal legal review (1 week), DocuSign routing (2–3 business days) — total approx. 2–3 weeks if there are no redlines.

Action items for Greenway:
- Confirm that Greenway will be controller for the EU processing and that Redwood is a processor for the described services.
- Provide Appendix 1 items (list of categories, processing purposes, transfer locations).
- Confirm whether you require a BAA for HIPAA-covered PHI.

If helpful, we can run a short call with Greenway counsel (Anna Ruiz) to walk through the appendix fields and the UK Addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
